questions.question: An assistant cites a superseded policy nobody deleted, and a consultant repeats wrong compliance guidance. When should that source have been caught?
options: After the incident, in the post-mortem
Never; old documents are harmless
In retrieval tuning months later
Before indexing, by ownership and freshness gates
questions.explanation: Governance failures predate embeddings. This lesson gates sources on authority, currency, consistency, and scope.

questions.question: What happens to a T3 source whose currency, consistency, and scope checks pass?
options: ADMIT, because passing the three objective checks outweighs its tier
DEFER, because T3 authority requires human review before admission
REJECT, because every informal source is permanently unusable
ADMIT only if it has no named owner
questions.explanation: T3 always fails the authority dimension by policy, but score_source uses DEFER for T3 so a human can review it. The other dimensions are still reported for that reviewer.

questions.question: Why is 'EU AI Act Compliance Checklist 2022' rejected by score_source?
options: It is T1, so named ownership is not allowed for compliance sources
Its case-study domain has a 9999-month expiry that the source exceeds
At 28 months old it exceeds the six-month compliance recency window
Its scope is always outside retrieval because compliance is not a domain
questions.explanation: The compliance window is six months. The candidate is 28 months old, so currency fails and the AND gate returns REJECT even though authority, consistency, and scope pass.

questions.question: What disposition does the 2019 case-study report receive when its owner, consistency, and scope are valid?
options: REJECT, because every source older than 36 months fails currency
DEFER, because historical reports cannot be authoritative
REJECT, because case studies have no recency window and therefore no score
ADMIT, because case_study uses the 9999-month recency window
questions.explanation: The case-study window is intentionally effectively unbounded. Seventy-two months is within 9999 months, so the T2 candidate passes all four dimensions and is admitted.

questions.question: What single dimension rejects the Team Wiki: RAG Architecture Notes candidate?
options: Currency, because 30 months exceeds the 24-month architecture window
Authority, because a T2 source can never have a named owner
Consistency, because every wiki note contradicts the corpus
Scope fit, because architecture is not a declared task domain
questions.explanation: The wiki has a named owner, is consistent, and is in scope. Its 30-month age exceeds the architecture window of 24 months, so currency is the failing dimension.

questions.question: What does the AND-gate policy imply when a source has strong scores on three dimensions but fails one?
options: The weighted average decides; three strong dimensions can compensate
The source is rejected for T1/T2 or deferred for T3, because one failed dimension is sufficient
The source is admitted but marked with a low-confidence citation
Only scope failure matters; authority and currency are advisory
questions.explanation: The policy is deliberately stricter than a weighted average. Any failed dimension rejects a T1/T2 candidate, while a T3 candidate is held for human review rather than silently admitted.
